title: Java Quiz
description: Fourteen questions covering the whole Java tutorial: the JVM and tools, syntax, types, operators, loops, methods, classes, inheritance, collections, generics, exceptions, strings and streams.

questions.question: What does the compiler `javac` produce from a `.java` file?
questions.explanation: javac writes a `.class` file containing bytecode for the JVM. Machine code is generated later, at run time, by the JVM's JIT compiler.
options: Machine code for the current CPU

questions.question: `java Hello.java` compiles and runs a single source file without leaving a `.class` file on disk.
questions.explanation: The source-file launcher, available since Java 11, compiles in memory and runs the program in one step.

questions.question: The keyword that makes a variable a constant which can be assigned only once is `___`.
questions.explanation: `final` prevents reassignment after the first assignment; attempting it gives `cannot assign a value to final variable`.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: `Integer.MAX_VALUE` is 2147483647. Adding one overflows silently and wraps around to the smallest int, -2147483648. Java never throws for plain int overflow; use `long` or `Math.addExact` when it matters.

questions.question: This prints `one` and then `two` although `code` is 1. Why?
questions.explanation: In the classic switch statement execution continues from the matching label until a `break`. `case 1` has no `break`, so it falls through into `case 2`. The arrow form `case 1 -> ...` never falls through.
options: `case 1` has no `break`, so execution falls through into `case 2`
The second label should be `case 1:` as well

questions.question: What does this loop print?
questions.explanation: `i` starts at 3 and the loop runs while `i > 0`, decrementing each time: 3, 2, 1. When `i` reaches 0 the condition fails. `print` does not add line breaks, so the digits appear on one line.

questions.question: A method declared `void` may still use `return;` to leave early.
questions.explanation: A bare `return;` without a value is allowed in a void method and ends it immediately. Only a `return` with a value is forbidden there.

questions.question: Inside a constructor, the keyword `___` refers to the object being created, as in `___.name = name;`.
questions.explanation: `this` is the reference to the current object. It is needed when a parameter has the same name as a field, otherwise the assignment would only touch the parameter.

questions.question: Which statement about Java interfaces is correct?
questions.explanation: Since Java 8 an interface may contain `default` methods with a body. A class may implement many interfaces, interface fields are implicitly `public static final` constants, and interfaces have no constructors.
options: An interface can declare `default` methods that have a body
A class can implement at most one interface
Interface fields are ordinary mutable instance variables
An interface can declare a constructor

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: A `TreeMap` keeps its keys sorted, so `a` comes before `b` regardless of insertion order. `merge("b", 5, Integer::sum)` adds 5 to the existing 1, giving 6.

questions.question: Type arguments are erased at run time, which is why `new T()` inside a generic class is not allowed.
questions.explanation: After compilation a `Box<String>` is just a `Box`; the JVM does not know what `T` was, so it cannot create an instance of it.

questions.question: Which of these is an unchecked exception?
questions.explanation: `IllegalArgumentException` extends `RuntimeException`, so the compiler does not force callers to handle it. `IOException`, `FileNotFoundException` and `InterruptedException` are checked and must be caught or declared.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: In `banana`, `an` first appears at index 1 and last at index 3. `replace` swaps every `a` for `o`, giving `bonono`. Strings are immutable, so `s` itself is unchanged, but the expression prints the new values.

questions.question: Why does this code not compile?
questions.explanation: Record components become `private final` fields. They can be read through the accessor `p.x()` but never reassigned, so javac reports `cannot assign a value to final variable x`. To get a changed point, create a new record: `new Point(5, p.y())`.
options: Record components are final, so `p.x = 5` cannot assign to one
Records must declare an explicit constructor
